title: Unified flywheel on real Emotion data
description:
## Purpose

Test the Unified Decision Flywheel on a REAL dataset where Jev starts weak, so the flywheel has something real to learn. **Headline claim tested: labels-only learning from disagreements** (the analyst sees which items were misclassified against the gold labels, with no human reasons).

Owner clarification: the explanation-driven loop (a stakeholder spots a misclassification and explains why it is wrong; the analyst turns that into a new rubric question) only works when such stakeholders exist. It CANNOT be evaluated on a static labeled dataset such as Emotion, where only labels exist. Its value can only be simulated here (optional L5, clearly labeled) or tested later with real reviewers in a pilot. The planted sports-vs-work corpus proved the machine works (A-c 0.83-0.87, A-c+F 0.85, D 0.89-0.92); real data was never tried. Replaces the Bias in Bios initiative (dropped: Jev already ~0.79, original loop +1.5 pts with a worse flip rate).

## Corpus

`dair-ai/emotion`, 6 classes (anger, fear, joy, love, sadness, surprise). Jev alone: zero-shot macro-F1 0.509 / acc 0.5915; best static retrieval (64/label) 0.649 / 0.694. Prepared: `studies/manifests/emotion.json`, HF cache `.data/huggingface/dair-ai___emotion`; Jev zero-shot answers for all 2,000 test items cached (`.data/dev/emotion.scoreboard2.sqlite`, jev-1.13.0), so the baseline is free.

## Approach

Parametrize `src/decision_flywheel_evaluations/unified_*.py` by a frozen `Corpus` config and `--corpus {planted,emotion}`; planted stays the default, byte-identical. 3 rounds x 150 labels from the pool; arms scored on dev-100 each round; nothing chosen on the final slice. Headline arms, labels only: 0 (free via cache), A (feature discovery from disagreements), F (optimized fixed list), F-rand (control), A+F (default product). In the harness A and A+F are the existing A-c and A-c+F arms run with an EMPTY comments input (A-c with no comments equals A). Optional D on the final slice only. Optional L5: simulated stakeholder explanations on A-c only, after the labels-only runs. Macro-F1 primary.

## Working rules (owner)

- Opus agents file plans in Kanbus (`kbs` only) before any build; builds are offline, small reviewed steps by Opus agents; the main session reviews, pushes and runs live stages.
- Small iterations (150 labels/round), development phase, no preregistration ceremony. Jev spend authorized within stated caps.
- Stop points where the owner looks before more is spent; ask the owner one plain question at a time, at the top of a message.
- Kanbus right_now summaries stay disabled in both repos.

## Cost cap

**Hard cumulative cap $10.** Upper bound ~13,000 Jev requests (~$1 per 1,000 few-shot requests; worst case ~$8); analyst (OpenAI gpt-6-luna) < $0.50; optional L0/L5 (simulated explanations) inside the same $10. Real spend lower because of caching.

## Caveats (carry into the results)

- Emotion test items were exposed in earlier project work: exploratory, not confirmatory.
- Labels came from hashtags: no consistent hidden rubric; noise ceiling (~0.7 plausible).
- Optional L5 only: the simulated reasons are rationalizations by a model that knows the gold label; reported as simulated, as a measure of the value of rubric communication, not as a property of the dataset.
- One seed. "surprise" is ~3.6% of test (dev-100 holds ~3-4): report per-class recall.

## What result changes what we build

- Labels-only A and A+F do not beat the free refit-only / static baselines (0.509 zero-shot, ~0.649 best static retrieval) on the final slice: the loop needs stakeholder feedback to help on noisy real labels (an argument for the stakeholder channel, not against the machine); stop the Emotion line.
- D clearly wins: dynamic retrieval becomes the default for multi-class tasks.
- F does not beat F-rand again: drop the list optimizer in favour of a random fixed list.
- The feature cap fires every round: larger rounds or one combined few-shot feature.
- Optional L5 (simulated explanations) is reported separately; it measures the value of rubric communication in simulation and changes no default by itself.
- Cached answers cannot be reused (hash mismatch): arm 0 costs ~$0.60 more on the final slice.

## Definition of done

Final slice scored for the arms with macro-F1, accuracy, per-class recall, confusion matrix, top-label Brier/ECE and paired bootstrap next to the free baselines; addendum in `studies/UNIFIED_FLYWHEEL_RESULTS.md` with the caveats; each rule above answered.

Approved plan: `~/.claude/plans/i-put-you-in-sprightly-penguin.md` (owner-approved 2026-10-01).

## Links

[DECISION_FLYWHEEL_DESIGN.md](https://github.com/AnthusAI/Decision-Flywheel-Evaluations/blob/main/studies/DECISION_FLYWHEEL_DESIGN.md); [UNIFIED_FLYWHEEL_RESULTS.md](https://github.com/AnthusAI/Decision-Flywheel-Evaluations/blob/main/studies/UNIFIED_FLYWHEEL_RESULTS.md)

comments.text: Owner clarification (2026-10-01): "In a pure, real dataset we're not going to get those explanations. The explanations are a way for stakeholders to communicate about rubrics by example over time rather than sitting down and writing down the perfect rubric in one perfect draft." And: "It only works if there are stakeholders who can spot a misclassification and explain why it's wrong. If we only have data then we can't do that." Consequences: the explanation-driven loop cannot be evaluated on a static labeled dataset such as Emotion. The headline run is LABELS ONLY and tests labels-only learning from disagreements: arms 0, A, F, F-rand, A+F (A and A+F = harness A-c and A-c+F with an empty comments input). Explanations become a separate optional experiment with SIMULATED stakeholder feedback (an LLM that knows the gold label; reasons are rationalizations), run only on A-c after the labels-only runs (new L5, ~1,600 + final), reported as simulated and as a measure of the value of rubric communication, not as a property of the dataset; real value needs real reviewers in a pilot. Re-chained: S1->S2->S3->S4->S6->S7->S8->L1->L2->L3 (labels-only path, no dependency on S5/L0); optional S5 (P3) blocked by S8; optional L0 (P3) blocked by S5 and L3; L5 (P3) blocked by L3, S5 and L0; L4 and Publish still blocked by L3. Decision rule added: if labels-only A and A+F do not beat the free refit-only/static baselines, the loop needs stakeholder feedback to help on noisy real labels (an argument for the stakeholder channel, not against the machine).
